name: Ultimate V60
author: James Hoffmann
summary: Hoffmann's well-known high-extraction V60. A big bloom, two main pours and a gentle stir and swirl to get a flat bed and an even drawdown.
tasteNotes: Balanced and sweet with good clarity. Expect a juicy, clean cup with ripe fruit and a long, sweet finish. Not thin and not harsh.

steps.note: Pour 2× the dose and swirl gently until everything is wet.
Pour to 60% of the water within about 30 s.
Pour to 100% a bit more gently. Finish by about 1:45.
Stir lightly once each way with a spoon, then give it a gentle swirl to flatten the bed.

tips: Use water just off the boil for light roasts.
Drawdown should finish around 3:30. If it runs longer, grind coarser. If it's faster, grind finer.
Rinse the paper well with hot water to remove paper taste and preheat the brewer.

name: Better 1-Cup V60
author: Based on James Hoffmann
summary: A single-cup method that splits the water into small, regular pulses. This keeps the bed temperature and agitation consistent with a small dose.
tasteNotes: Sweet and clean with lively but rounded acidity. Medium body and a clear, transparent flavour that shows off the origin.
grind: Medium-fine, slightly finer than a big batch (about 550–700 µm)

steps.note: Swirl gently so every ground is wet.
Gentle pour in small circles.
Last pour, then let it drain.
One gentle swirl to flatten the bed.

tips: Small doses lose heat quickly, so use very hot water.
Aim for a drawdown that finishes around 3:00.

name: 4:6 Method
author: Tetsu Kasuya (WBrC 2016)
summary: Five equal pours of 60 g every 45 s with a coarse grind. The first 40% of the water controls the acidity–sweetness balance. The last 60% controls strength.
tasteNotes: Very sweet, round and balanced with soft acidity and a clean, easy finish. Very forgiving thanks to the coarse grind.
grind: Coarse, like coarse sea salt (about 900–1100 µm)

steps.note: Pour 1 of 5. Part of the first 40% (balance).
Pour 2: completes the 40% phase.
Pour 3: strength phase begins.
Pour 4
Pour 5, the last pour.
Remove the dripper at 3:30 even if some water is left.

tips: For more sweetness, make the first pour smaller (e.g. 50 g then 70 g).
For more acidity, make the first pour larger (e.g. 70 g then 50 g).
For a stronger cup, split the last 60% into 3 pours. For a lighter cup, use 2 pours.
Light roasts: 93 °C. Medium: 88 °C. Dark: 83 °C.

name: 4:6 Sweet
author: Tetsu Kasuya, sweetness variant
summary: The 4:6 method with a smaller first pour and a larger second pour. This shifts the balance toward sweetness.
tasteNotes: Extra sweet and syrupy with softer, rounder acidity than the standard 4:6. Great for bright, acidic washed coffees.
grind: Coarse, like coarse sea salt (about 900–1100 µm)

steps.note: Smaller first pour = more sweetness.
Larger second pour (70 g).
Remove the dripper at 3:30.

tips: If it's still too sharp, go to 40 g / 80 g for the first two pours.

name: Rao V60
author: Scott Rao
summary: A large 3× bloom, then a steady high pour that keeps the slurry level high. Finished with the famous 'Rao spin' for a perfectly flat bed.
tasteNotes: Very clean and transparent with high clarity and sweetness. Delicate florals and fruit come through. Light-to-medium body.

steps.note: Bloom with 3× the dose. Gently dig or stir so there are no dry clumps.
Pour steadily in spirals and keep the slurry level high.
Continue to the full weight.
Rao spin: one firm swirl to flatten the bed.

tips: A flat bed at the end means even extraction.
Use a fast-flowing paper (e.g. Hario tabbed or Sibarist).

name: Everyday 3-Pour
author: Classic
summary: A simple, quick daily V60: a short bloom, a small second pour and one big final pour.
tasteNotes: Balanced and approachable with medium body, gentle acidity and caramel sweetness. A reliable daily cup.

steps.note: Wet all the grounds evenly.
Pour 50 g.
Pour the final 150 g in slow spirals.

tips: Aim to finish drawdown between 2:30 and 3:00.

name: Switch Hybrid
author: Tetsu Kasuya
summary: Starts as a percolation with hot water and finishes as an immersion with cooler water. Hot water brings clarity and acidity. Cool water brings sweetness and body.
tasteNotes: Very sweet with a rounded, syrupy body and soft, gentle acidity. A dessert-like cup with almost no bitterness.

steps.note: Valve OPEN. Pour with 90 °C water.
Still open, hot water.
CLOSE the valve. Pour to the full weight with about 70 °C water.
OPEN the valve and let it drain.

tips: Prepare a second kettle or let the water cool to about 70 °C for the immersion stage.
Use the 03 size Switch or a V60 02 paper in the Switch 02.

name: Switch Full Immersion
author: Classic
summary: Close the valve, add all the water, steep, then release. Very consistent and forgiving, like a clean French press.
tasteNotes: Round, sweet and comforting with fuller body and muted acidity. Very easy to repeat, rarely harsh.

steps.note: Valve CLOSED. Pour all water gently, wetting all grounds.
Gently stir to break up any dry clumps.
OPEN the valve and let it drain.

tips: Steep longer for more strength. Grind finer for more extraction.

name: Flat-Bottom Pulse
author: Classic Kalita Wave
summary: Steady pulses into a flat-bottom dripper (Kalita Wave, Orea, April). The flat bed gives an even, forgiving extraction.
tasteNotes: Even and sweet with a bit more body than a V60. Balanced acidity and a smooth finish.

steps.note: Wet all the grounds evenly and let it degas.
Last pour, then let it drain.

tips: Pour in the centre and avoid hitting the walls.

name: Lance Hedrick 1-2-1 V60
author: Lance Hedrick
summary: High-clarity method with a 3× bloom, one main single-stream pour with low agitation, and a gentle swirl to settle the bed. Emphasizes clean fruit acidity and sweetness.
tasteNotes: Vibrant and transparent with explosive sweetness, sparkling fruit acidity and a delicate, silky body.

steps.note: Pour 3× the dose quickly and swirl vigorously to wet all grounds completely.
Pour steadily in a single stream with low agitation until you reach 250 g.
Gentle swirl to wash down high grounds and settle a flat bed.

tips: Keep the kettle spout close to the water surface to minimize agitation and maximize sweetness.
Ideal for washed Kenyans, Ethiopians, and Geshas.

name: Orea V4 High Flow
author: Matteo D'Ottavio (Orea UK)
summary: Fast extraction flat-bottom method for the Orea V3/V4. Exploits the fast open drainage with 3 rapid concentric pulses for ultra-clean sweetness and vibrant fruit notes.
tasteNotes: Punchy fruit notes, intense sweetness and a juicy mouthfeel with round acidity and zero astringency.

steps.note: Pour 50 g bloom in 10 s. Swirl gently.
Pour fast in circles from inside out up to 150 g.
Pour central stream to 250 g. Let it drain.

tips: Fast drawdown of 2:00 to 2:20 is typical with the open-bottom base.
Works best with Kalita 185 wave filters or Sibarist fast papers.

name: Orea 4-Pour Pulse
author: The Coffee Chronicler
summary: Four evenly spaced pulses that allow the water to drain almost completely between pours, maximizing extraction consistency without clogging.
tasteNotes: Very approachable, sweet, well-rounded cup with balanced body and gentle stone fruit acidity.

steps.note: First pour: 50 g bloom.
Second pour: 60 g circular pour.
Third pour: 65 g circular pour.
Final pour: 65 g center pour.

tips: Let the slurry drain down almost completely before starting each subsequent pulse.

name: Origami WBrC Champion
author: Du Jianing (World Brewers Cup 2019)
summary: The 2019 World Brewers Cup winning recipe using the Origami dripper. Segmented pours that leverage Origami's deep vertical ribs for steady flow and aromatic complexity.
tasteNotes: Extraordinary floral aroma, bright sweet citrus, layered berry complexity and silky texture.

steps.note: Gentle 40 g bloom in the center, blooming for 40 s.
Pour 60 g in small outwards spirals.
Pour 60 g in medium spirals.
Final 80 g pour in steady center stream.

tips: Use Kalita 185 wave paper in the Origami for sweeter, rounder cups, or conical V60 paper for higher acidity.
Maintain a low pouring height to avoid over-agitating the fines.

name: Switch 'God Recipe'
author: The Coffee Chronicler
summary: Half percolation, half immersion. Opens with a classic V60 bloom and pour for floral aroma, then closes the valve for a rich immersion that boosts sweetness and body.
tasteNotes: Exceptional balance: bright citrus top notes with a creamy, chocolatey body and sweet brown sugar finish.

steps.note: Valve OPEN. 60 g bloom with 93 °C water.
Valve OPEN. Pour 60 g in gentle circles.
CLOSE valve.
Pour remaining 130 g into the closed Switch.
OPEN valve at 2:00 and let all coffee draw down.

tips: For a lighter, juicier cup, use 85 °C water for the immersion phase.
Drawdown after opening typically finishes between 2:45 and 3:15.

name: Switch Water-First
author: James Hoffmann
summary: Pours hot water into the closed switch BEFORE adding ground coffee. This prevents fines from settling into the filter and guarantees zero clogging and ultra-consistent drawdown.
tasteNotes: Incredibly smooth, clean, syrupy body, round acidity and intense dark chocolate sweetness.

steps.note: Valve CLOSED. Pour all 300 g boiling water into the dripper first.
Add 18 g ground coffee into the water and stir gently to submerge all grounds.
At 2:00, OPEN valve and let it draw down.

tips: Because water goes in first, coffee will not clog the paper, resulting in a fast 45-second drawdown.

name: Kasuya Devil's Recipe
author: Tetsu Kasuya
summary: Designed specifically for dark or medium-dark roasts to eliminate all bitterness and astringency while highlighting rich chocolate and caramel sweetness.
tasteNotes: Deep, velvety chocolate, toasted almond sweetness, heavy syrupy mouthfeel and zero bitterness or dry astringency.

steps.note: Low temp bloom at 82 °C. Gently swirl to wet all grounds.
Pour gently to 120 g in small concentric circles.
Pour to 180 g.
Pour to 240 g.
Final pour to 280 g.
Remove dripper at 3:30 even if some water remains.

tips: Strictly keep water temperature between 80 °C and 83 °C.
Do not let the final astringent drops enter your cup; remove the dripper before it fully drains.

name: Orea V4 Big Bloom
author: BrewLog Barista
summary: Demonstrating a 4× bloom on flat-bottom Orea V4 with open bottom plug for high extraction and clarity.
tasteNotes: Very clean, bright berry acidity, transparent floral notes.

steps.note: Pour 60 g bloom, swirl 3 times.
Pour fast spiral to 150 g.
Pour center stream to 250 g.

tips: Drawdown should finish around 2:10.

name: Origami Wave Pulse
author: BrewLog Barista
summary: Using Kalita Wave 185 papers inside the Origami dripper for enhanced sweetness and velvety body.
tasteNotes: Honey sweetness, stone fruit, mellow orange acidity and velvety body.

steps.note: Gentle 50 g bloom.
Pour in concentric circles to 120 g.
Pour to 190 g.
Final center pour to 250 g.

tips: Rinse Wave paper carefully so pleats don't collapse.

name: Switch Blooming Immersion
author: BrewLog Barista
summary: Switch recipe combining an open-valve bloom for vibrant acidity with a closed full immersion steep for body.
tasteNotes: Rich cocoa, plum sweetness and round syrupy mouthfeel.

steps.note: Valve OPEN. Bloom with 60 g water.
CLOSE valve.
Fill to 280 g and let steep.
OPEN valve at 2:00 to drain.

tips: A gentle swirl at 1:45 helps sink any floating grounds before release.

name: My Custom Pour-Over
author: Home Barista
summary: Crisp, sweet, and balanced cup with floral aroma and vibrant citrus acidity.
tasteNotes: Bergamot, jasmine blossoms, honey sweetness and juicy peach.

steps.note: Pour evenly and gently swirl to saturate all grounds.
Pour in concentric circles from center out.
Final gentle pour to target weight; gentle swirl at the end.
Drawdown finished. Remove dripper and enjoy!

tips: Rinse paper filter before adding coffee to wash out paper taste and pre-heat dripper.
Keep kettle spout close to the slurry to minimize turbulent splashing.

name: Classic Espresso 1:2
author: Traditional
summary: The standard starting point: 18 g in, 36 g out in about 28 seconds at 9 bar. Dial in with the grind first, then fine-tune the ratio.
tasteNotes: Sweet, syrupy and balanced with a long finish. Medium and darker roasts shine; light roasts can taste sharp at this ratio.
grind: Fine (espresso). Adjust so the shot takes 25–30 s.

steps.note: Start the shot. The first drops should appear after 5–8 s.
Stop the shot just before 36 g in the cup.

tips: Distribute (WDT) and tamp level: most sour-and-bitter shots are channeling.
Change one thing at a time: grind first, then ratio, then temperature.

name: Ristretto 1:1.5
author: Traditional
summary: A short, concentrated shot: 18 g in, 27 g out. Great for milk drinks and darker roasts.
tasteNotes: Intense, heavy and sweet with less bitterness than a full shot. Thick body, low clarity.
grind: Fine, a touch finer than for a 1:2 shot.

steps.note: Start the shot.
Stop at 27 g.

tips: If it turns sour, grind finer rather than running it longer.

name: Lungo 1:3
author: Traditional
summary: A longer shot: 18 g in, 54 g out with a slightly coarser grind. Lighter and more open than a classic shot.
tasteNotes: Lighter body and more clarity, with more fruit and acidity. Can turn bitter if it runs too slow.
grind: Fine, a few steps coarser than for a 1:2 shot.

steps.note: Start the shot.
Stop at 54 g.

tips: Bitter or drying? Grind coarser or drop the temperature by 1–2 °C.

name: Turbo Shot
author: Cameron et al. (2020)
summary: Coarser grind, lower pressure, fast shot: 18 g in, 50 g out in about 16 s at 6 bar. Even extraction with fewer channels, very repeatable.
tasteNotes: Clear, sweet and juicy with bright acidity. Made for light and medium-light roasts.
grind: Medium-fine, much coarser than a classic shot (between espresso and AeroPress).

steps.note: Start the shot at about 6 bar.
Stop at 50 g.

tips: Needs pressure control (e.g. GaggiMate, a flow-control paddle or a lever).
Sour? Grind finer in small steps; the shot gets slower but stays even.

name: Allongé 1:4
author: Scott Rao
summary: A long, hot shot for very light roasts: 18 g in, 72 g out at 96 °C. Somewhere between espresso and filter.
tasteNotes: Tea-like clarity and florals with sweet, bright acidity. Light body, no heaviness.
grind: Fine to medium-fine, coarser than a classic shot.

steps.note: Start the shot.
Stop at 72 g.

tips: Only for very light, high-grown coffees. Use the hottest water your machine allows.
